recipe.positive: Visual style (follow exactly): Art Deco machine-age decorative technique: strict geometric axial order and symmetry, stepped lines, chevron, sunburst or fan and zigzag motifs, streamlined stylised forms, crisp hard-edged flat gouache shapes with thin gold linework, layered stepped silhouettes and parallel speed lines, an elegant luxurious mood. Gold stays as thin line accents only. Figures, faces, hair, clothing and objects come only from the current brief, including modern clothing and short hair; the geometric order applies to composition and background, so no period costume is imposed on the people. Default colour tendency when no palette is requested: Black, deep teal/emerald, burgundy or navy, cream, with gold accent lines. Controlled, not rainbow. If the brief explicitly requests a recolour, retain the same limited colour roles, line contrast and material character.
hard_constraints: Forms are geometric, straight and hard-edged, with flat colour and no photographic shading.
Gold is thin linework only and never a broad metallic surface.

anchor.isolation: Take only the material qualities from this original technique study: matte opaque hard-edged gouache surface, fine paper tooth inside flat planes, and thin non-reflective gold ink line quality. "Material only" does not mean discarding the written Art Deco recipe: the recipe still governs composition and ornament. Every finished picture must keep a clear, visible axial ornamental order, freshly drawn for the current brief: small symmetric fans or sunburst segments, stepped bands and chevron/herringbone runs that frame the view or follow the architecture or scene structure given in the brief. Do not reduce the requested scene to plain rectangles or a generic modern polygon poster, and do not let a single-vanishing-point scene replace that ornamental order. Concrete objects, people and props on the left and right need not be mirrored, and the order is not a head-count or stall-count symmetry; it lives in the framing, architectural trim, eaves, windows, borders and background. Keep the ornament proportionate so it does not overpower the factual content, with no broad metallic areas or gradients. This study is a material proof, not a layout or a source of subjects. Do not copy its diagonal corner slabs, isolated central stair stroke, ray positions, chevron crop, gold-stripe placement, polygon silhouettes, intersections, colour blocks pressed across the whole frame, or overall arrangement, and do not drift into generic Bauhaus or Memphis. Redraw every mark and composition freshly. Add no reference swatches, panels, grids, labels, stamps or writing, and add no figurative objects, characters or emblems that the brief does not request. People, animals, props and the scene, including count, age, modern clothing, expression, pose and interaction, come only from the current brief; the reference supplies none of them. If the brief explicitly requests a palette, use that palette for the colour roles instead of the reference hues, keeping the restricted roles and matte material. Add only the exact requested text when the brief asks for text.
